cropping.notes: Summer kinds crop in June and July: pick fully red fruit with the stalk every day or two.

lookOutFor: Tuck straw under the fruit to keep it clean. Replace plants every three years.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Young plants eaten, especially on damp nights
pests.control: Protect young plants and check for slugs after dark; encourage birds, frogs and beetles.

pests.name: Grey mould
pests.signs: Fluffy grey mould on the fruit
pests.control: Pick off affected fruit and give plants space for air.

wintering.notes: Cut off the old leaves after fruiting.

flowering: Tuck straw under the plants to keep fruit clean, and net against birds.
harvesting: Pick fruit when fully red, ideally in the warmth of the day.

source: Check against: RHS – strawberries; nursery label

cropping.notes: Summer kinds fruit June–July, autumn kinds August–October.

lookOutFor: Grow summer kinds along wires; plant canes 5 cm deep and cut them to 25 cm.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

pests.name: Raspberry beetle
pests.signs: Small grubs inside ripe fruit
pests.control: Lightly fork the soil round the canes in winter so birds can find the pupae.

wintering.notes: Summer kinds: cut fruited canes to the ground after picking. Autumn kinds: cut all canes down in late winter.

source: Check against: RHS – raspberries; nursery label

lookOutFor: Thornless kinds are easier to train along wires or a fence.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

wintering.notes: Cut out the canes that fruited; tie in the new ones.

source: Check against: RHS – blackberries; nursery label

lookOutFor: Plant 5 cm deeper than it grew in the pot, so new shoots come from below ground.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

pests.name: Big bud mite
pests.signs: Swollen, round buds in winter
pests.control: Pick off and remove swollen buds.

wintering.notes: Prune in winter, removing about a third of the oldest stems.

source: Check against: RHS – blackcurrants; nursery label

lookOutFor: Copes with a north-facing wall; can be trained as a cordon.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

pests.name: Sawfly larvae
pests.signs: Leaves stripped by green caterpillar-like larvae
pests.control: Check under the lowest leaves from spring and pick the larvae off by hand.

wintering.notes: Prune in winter to an open goblet shape.

source: Check against: RHS – redcurrants; nursery label

cropping.notes: Thin in late May for cooking; leave the rest to ripen.

pests.name: Sawfly larvae
pests.signs: Leaves stripped by green caterpillar-like larvae
pests.control: Check under the lowest leaves from spring and pick the larvae off by hand.

pests.name: American gooseberry mildew
pests.signs: White, then brown, coating on fruit and shoots
pests.control: Prune to keep the bush open and airy; choose resistant kinds.

wintering.notes: Prune in winter to an open goblet shape.

source: Check against: RHS – gooseberries; nursery label

lookOutFor: Water with rainwater: tap water slowly makes the soil less acid. Two kinds fruit better than one.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

source: Check against: RHS – blueberries; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pull, don’t cut, the stalks. Leave new plants a year to settle, and stop picking by late July.

lookOutFor: The leaves are poisonous (check): eat only the stalks.
Plant crowns with the buds just at the surface.
source: Check against: RHS – rhubarb; nursery label

lookOutFor: The rootstock decides the size: choose a dwarfing one for small gardens.
Most need another apple nearby to pollinate them.

pests.name: Codling moth
pests.signs: Grubs in the core of the fruit
pests.control: Hang pheromone traps in May; clear up fallen fruit.

pests.name: Apple scab
pests.signs: Dark, scabby patches on fruit and leaves
pests.control: Clear up fallen leaves in autumn; choose resistant kinds.

source: Check against: RHS – apples; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick while still firm and ripen indoors.

lookOutFor: Flowers early, so frost can catch the blossom: avoid frost pockets.

pests.name: Pear rust
pests.signs: Bright orange spots on the leaves
pests.control: Remove affected leaves; it rarely harms the crop.

source: Check against: RHS – pears; nursery label

lookOutFor: Prune only in summer, to avoid silver leaf disease.

pests.name: Plum moth
pests.signs: Pink grubs in ripe fruit
pests.control: Hang pheromone traps in May.

source: Check against: RHS – plums; nursery label

lookOutFor: Prune in summer only. Choose a self-fertile kind if you have room for just one.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Fruit pecked or stripped as it ripens
pests.control: Net plants, or grow them in a fruit cage, before the fruit colours.

source: Check against: RHS – cherries; nursery label

lookOutFor: Restrict the roots in a pit or a large pot, or it grows leaves instead of fruit.

wintering.notes: Fleece the young fruitlets on cold nights. Remove larger figs in autumn: they won’t ripen.

source: Check against: RHS – figs; nursery label

lookOutFor: Needs a sunny wall or a greenhouse in most of the UK.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.signs: White powder on the leaves
pests.control: Water at the roots in dry spells and give plants space for air to move.

pests.name: Birds
